newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees sales boost lifting Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees sales boost lifting Q4 results.

text.p: Xerox Inc chief executive Paul Allaire said the company's rebound from a disappointing third quarter that blindsided investors will come from tight expense control and a more productive sale force.

In a conference call with analysts and institutional investors, he said "Our (third quarter) revenue growth was slightly lower than what we expected and SGA was slightly higher than expected and the combination the two gave profits that were off expected levels."
He said he expects greater productivity in the fourth quarter as the sales force gains experience.
He also said the company will attempt to cut selling, general and administrative expenses (SGA), but has no intention to cut the size of the sales force.

"We did not get out of the new hires what we expected to in the third quarter. With training, we will start to see some improvement ... and to ensure (sales force) stability and address turnover problems, we have increased sales compensation levels as well," Allaire said.

Barry Romeril, chief financial officer, told listeners that the company's $1 billion share buyback is intact, with the level of stock purchases "loosley correlated" to proceeds Xerox would get in the sale of its insurance units.
Xerox had agreed to sell the Talegen insurance operation to buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis & Roberts for $2.7 billion, but the deal was killed unexpectedly last month.

"We will be looking at what happens in the market (to determine repurchases). We have the program and it remains in place and we will factor in Talegen proceeds as a major influence on the size of purchase," Romeril said.
In February, the Xerox board approved buyback of up to $1 billion of common stock. By September 30, 5 million shares had been purchased or $232 million.
